subject: Urgent: unexpected 429 spike after project tier reassignment
messages:
From: Alejandro Cortez <alejandro@healthspark.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@healthspark.io
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden 429s + timeouts across our project

Hi Jasmine —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and client-side timeouts at ~08:45 PT for all requests originating from our project ID: proj-hs-221. Error rates jumped from ~0.5% to ~18% and many background jobs are failing. We rolled a small backoff but the retry storms keep amplifying the failures.

Key symptoms:
- 429s across generation endpoints (stream and non-stream)
- spikes in latency (p95 from 120ms -> 1.8s)
- repeated ClientRetry backoff loops on our side

We've attached a short snapshot from our side (log lines + request ids) and can share more. Can you check whether any quota changes or tier reassignments happened this morning?

This is impacting our production flows — we need immediate mitigation and an ETA for a fix.

Thanks,
Alejandro
Platform Ops — HealthSpark
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Alejandro Cortez <alejandro@healthspark.io>, ops@healthspark.io
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s + timeouts across our project

Alejandro —

Thanks for the heads up and the log snippet. I'm pulling Priyom (runtime) and Neha (AM) in now.

Immediate ask: can you forward the most recent request IDs (request-id/trace-id) and the exact project id used in calls? We'll run a rate/time series and look for quota assignments. In parallel, Priyom — please check recent tiering/assignment jobs; there was a roll this morning to propagate updated org-tier maps.

Short-term mitigation plan (we'll confirm actions in 15–30m):
- Prioritize healthspark traffic to fallback org-tier if project-level limits were misapplied
- Temporarily increase the project's token bucket to stop immediate 429s (emergency knob)
- Apply circuit-breaker rules on our side to avoid retry amplification while we repair mapping

Neha: I'll keep the customer updated. Alejandro, apologies for the hit — we'll treat this as an incident with exec visibility if needed.

— Jasmine
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Alejandro Cortez <alejandro@healthspark.io>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s + timeouts across our project

Alejandro / team —

I pulled the serving logs and the tiering audit trail. Quick summary:
- Around 08:30 PT a batch job that re-applied project->org tier mappings ran (internal job id: tier-propagate-20261106-3).
- For proj-hs-221 the mapping post-job shows an unintended downgrade: project lost its dedicated project-tier override and reverted to a lower default org-tier with a ~10x lower token rate.
- Our rate limiter enforces the lower token budget immediately which explains the 429 spike.

Root cause hypothesis: a migration bug in the propagation script treats unset project-level overrides as explicit low-tier values when a customer is in a mixed-tier org (we missed a null-check). That case only happens for orgs with mixed reserved/dedicated projects — explains why this didn't show in staging.

Immediate actions taken (already executing):
1) Opened INF-4521 and ran an emergency rollback of the last tier-propagate job for the HealthSpark org.
2) Applied a temporary project-level override for proj-hs-221 to restore previous token capacity.
3) Adjusted rate-limiter to prefer explicit project overrides over propagated defaults while we patch.

I've attached a rate snapshot and the top request traces showing the 429s (error_trace_1600.log). Expected customer-facing effect: traffic should start recovering within one token-refresh window (approx 60–90s) after override is active; p95 latency should drop back to baseline once retries quiesce.

Follow-ups:
- We're preparing a code change to fix the null-check and a targeted test to catch mixed-tier orgs.
- I recommend we keep a temporary elevated bucket for HealthSpark for 24h while we validate the fix.

I'll post updates to the Jira ticket and the incident channel.

— Priyom
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Marissa —

Quick exec summary for awareness / next steps: HealthSpark (proj-hs-221) experienced an operational outage window from ~08:30–08:46 PT due to an unintended downgrade in project token capacity after a tier-propagation job. Impacted customer latency and caused retry amplification; they reported ~18% 429 rate at peak and background jobs failing.

Actions taken:
- Priyom rolled back the propagation job and applied a project-level override; traffic resumed within ~60s of mitigation.
- Engineering will push a bugfix (null-check + unit/integration coverage) and extend testing for mixed-tier orgs.
- We'll keep an elevated token bucket for 24 hours and monitor the health metrics closely.

Customer asks: clear timeline, RCA, formal postmortem, and confirmation of credits if any SLA thresholds were crossed.

Proposed next steps for leadership:
1) Approve 24h elevated bucket for HealthSpark (NO cost cap requested yet).
2) Offer a one-week credit hold for background job retries if SLA breach confirmed.
3) Prioritize INF-4521 in next hotfix deploy (ETA 24h).

I'll draft a short postmortem and the communications to HealthSpark once we agree on credit policy.

— Neha
